proof_state.history_validation: ledger reopening validates receipt ID, monotonic sequence and the referenced claims as latest at the recorded claim_count

valid_transitions: all required signed input claims are current while the exclusive ledger lock is held
Burn executes the graph and the host observes output shape and f32 values
the host atomically commits the receipt to the same private ledger before replying
a failed receipt commit returns an error; no success response or durable receipt is asserted
later input revisions cannot rewrite an earlier valid historical receipt
limits: A failed receipt commit can occur after numerical execution; the runner does not claim numerical rollback or exactly-once side effects.
JSON numeric values cannot distinguish negative zero from positive zero; use output_f32_le_base64 for exact output comparison.
A content hash detects accidental modification but a privileged writer of the host ledger can rewrite its history.
Program identity excludes mutable layer state; this receipt commits the observed output and does not claim independent numerical implementation.
A receipt can supply exact output bytes to the Node durable state-handoff path; the handoff record does not authorize actions or state promotion.
A 50,000-receipt or 32 MiB ledger limit fails closed for new durable run receipts.

authority.parent_receipt: durable host ledger record of an observed Burn-backed run
authority.payload: exact little-endian f32 bytes from that receipt output
authority.child_input: configured issuer signature over the target state input and its values
authority.handoff_record: host ledger transition; it does not authorize an agent action

valid_transition: runner retrieves parent receipt by receipt_id from the same subject-bound ledger
caller supplies the receipt output_f32_le_base64 as a state input payload
host checks exact shape and f32 digest equality before binding
issuer signature verifies the child state claim for the target program manifest
host atomically commits the child input claim and parent-to-child handoff record
later execution receipt references the handoff record and its child input claim
the same subject/source/logical state port/branch must advance to a strictly newer parent receipt sequence

branching.forking: caller chooses another bounded handoff_branch_id to start an independent state lineage
branching.replay_policy: a receipt cannot rewind or repeat within the same subject/source/logical port/branch

transport.shape: the exact parent output shape; rank 4 with positive u32 dimensions

limits: Only role=state can consume a parent execution receipt.
The child claim must satisfy the target manifest and configured issuer policy.
The host checks value continuity; the original receipt ID is a host ledger reference, not an issuer signature over causal meaning.
Cross-subject handoffs are rejected; direct WASM APIs bypass this Node host transition.

definition.purpose: Persist the causal relation baseline execution receipt -> verified branch receipt -> promoted candidate checkpoint without giving the host or reference machine authority to select a branch automatically.

authority.numerical_verification: WASM Burn reference machine branch receipt

protocol.phase_1_begin: before mutation, beginPromotion validates the committed baseline host receipt, exact compact WASM branch receipt bytes, equivalent=true, state diff, candidate ProgramBundle digest and candidate program identity, then commits a pending intent
protocol.phase_2_commit: caller explicitly invokes CheckpointBranchSet.commitBranchByReceipt; this contract does not perform or authorize that selection
protocol.phase_3_complete: after mutation, completePromotion accepts only exact promoted ProgramBundle bytes and program identity matching the pending candidate and appends a completion event
protocol.crash_semantics: a crash or failure after begin but before complete leaves a durable pending intent and never implies that promotion succeeded

validation.baseline: must be a committed burn-research.host-execution-receipt.v2 for the same host subject and its exact state checkpoint/program identity must match the branch receipt baseline
validation.branch_receipt: must be exact compact burn-research.checkpoint-branch-verification.v1 bytes whose outer SHA-256 receipt digest reproduces, equivalent=true, promotion_authorized=false, and whose nested Burn verifier receipt is passing
validation.candidate: begin and complete both hash exact ProgramBundle bytes; the digest must equal candidate_state_checkpoint_bytes_sha256
validation.state_diff: baseline/candidate bundle digests must agree with the branch receipt and semantic_equivalence_asserted must remain false
validation.restart: all intent and completion IDs plus branch receipt bytes are revalidated on every ledger load

storage.candidate_bundle_retention: digest only; checkpoint bytes are not duplicated in the lineage ledger

limits: A completed lineage event proves that the host observed exact candidate bytes and identity after a pending promotion intent; it does not prove external input truth or general model equivalence.
The WASM branch receipt covers only the test vectors supplied to MultiInputVerificationCases.
The sidecar ledger is a host trust root; hashes are tamper-evident correlation values, not signatures or action authorization.
This checkpoint does not expose a JSON Lines branch-selection API and does not let the host choose among branches.
Pending events are intentionally preserved as indeterminate after crashes; they must never be interpreted as successful promotions.

definition.purpose: Unify existing graph-operation contracts into a discoverable constructible-operation pool and resolve declarative graph plans before any executor is invoked.

pool.query_boundary: caller intent is taken only from own properties; inherited prototype properties are ignored; non-object and array queries are REJECTED with INVALID_PARAMETER
pool.selection: query returns all compatible or deferred candidates; no ranking or recommendation
pool.live_registry_instance_inventory: deferred; this v1 does not enumerate initialized LayerRegistry identities

declarative_plan.dependency_policy: steps may reference declared inputs or outputs from earlier steps only

resolution_status.RESOLVED: one exact operation identity is selected for every step and all modeled static contracts are satisfied
resolution_status.AMBIGUOUS: more than one operation candidate remains or required caller/agent information is missing
resolution_status.DEFERRED: operation identity is known but one or more authoritative conditions cannot be proven until canonical constructor, registry, or Burn/runtime preflight
resolution_status.REJECTED: a known contract violation makes the declarative plan inadmissible

proof_matrix: inherited selector properties do not become caller intent
malformed pool query -> REJECTED with INVALID_PARAMETER
known operation with unmodeled authoritative static rule -> DEFERRED
canonical layout subset compatibility is preserved from agent-layout-contracts.v1
resolved plan remains execution_authorized=false and mutation=none

invariants: the registry is derived from existing machine-readable contracts rather than becoming a new numerical source of truth
pool queries never rank or select an operation on behalf of the agent
pool query intent is derived only from own properties and never from Object prototype inheritance
malformed pool queries return a machine-readable REJECTED result rather than throwing as caller-input errors
RESOLVED does not authorize execution and does not bypass AgentLayerSpec constructor validation, LayerRegistry binding, graph preflight, or Burn
unknown or dynamic layout and shape semantics become DEFERRED rather than REJECTED unless an existing contract proves incompatibility
semantic output roles remain caller or agent declarations and are never inferred from numerical layer type
known layout, axis, arity, dependency, parameter-type, and graph-capacity mismatches fail before execution
the v1 pool enumerates constructible operation types, not live initialized LayerRegistry instances
future_extensions: live LayerRegistry instance inventory and identity-aware pool filtering

authority_boundaries.wasm: Rust/Burn reference machine owns numerical execution and WASM capability descriptions
authority_boundaries.node_host: Node contracts describe optional trust, replay, receipt, state handoff, durable promotion-lineage, and operation-planning projections outside the WASM export surface
authority_boundaries.operation_registry: constructible operation discovery and declarative plan resolution are read-only host projections; AgentLayerSpec, AgentGraphBuilder, LayerRegistry and Burn remain authoritative
authority_boundaries.preflight: readiness and compatibility do not grant external action authority

fingerprint.canonicalization: UTF-8 compact JSON with recursively sorted object keys and preserved array order; fingerprint field omitted
fingerprint.authority: artifact consistency and correlation only; not a signature, provenance proof, or action authorization
